domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation. The status field drives all workflow transitions and balance impacts.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — Employee has created but not yet submitted the request. Editable. No balance impact. Transitions: submit() → SUBMITTED, cancel() → CANCELLED.

SUBMITTED — Request has been submitted and is pending manager review. Immutable except for status transitions. No balance impact yet. Transitions: approve() → APPROVED, reject() → REJECTED, cancel() → CANCELLED.
APPROVED — Manager has approved the request. Balance is deducted. Immutable. Transitions: cancel() → CANCELLED.
REJECTED — Manager has rejected the request. Terminal state. No balance impact. No further transitions.
CANCELLED — Request was cancelled by the employee (or admin). If cancelled from APPROVED, balance is restored. Terminal state. No further transitions.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Each LeaveType has exactly one active LeavePolicy at any time. Governs entitlement, accrual behaviour, notice requirements, and whether manager approval is needed.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Policy is in effect and governs leave requests of its type. Transitions: deactivate() → INACTIVE.
INACTIVE — Policy is no longer in effect. Does not apply to new requests. Existing approved requests under this policy remain valid. Transitions: activate() → ACTIVE.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific policy and fiscal year. Deductions occur on approval; restorations occur on cancellation-from-approved. The remainingDays is a derived invariant: totalEntitlement - usedDays.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Balance is in effect for the current fiscal year. Accruals and deductions apply. Transitions: close() → CLOSED.
CLOSED — Balance belongs to a past fiscal year. No further accruals or deductions. Read-only for audit/history. No further transitions.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. Owns leave requests and balances. The managerId establishes the approval hierarchy: a manager approves leave for their direct reports.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Employee is currently employed and eligible for leave. Transitions: terminate() → TERMINATED.
INACTIVE — Employee is on leave of absence or suspended. May have restricted leave eligibility. Transitions: reactivate() → ACTIVE, terminate() → TERMINATED.
TERMINATED — Employment has ended. No leave eligibility. Terminal state. No further transitions.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type has its own LeavePolicy governing entitlement, accrual, and approval rules. The type on a LeaveRequest determines which policy and balance are consulted.

business_rules: LeaveRequest status transitions are strictly governed by the lifecycle state machine: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → {APPROVED | REJECTED}; any non-terminal state → CANCELLED. No other transitions are valid. Attempting an invalid transition is a domain error. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest.status appears, not only here]

The number of leave days consumed by a LeaveRequest is calculated as: (endDate - startDate) + 1, inclusive of both start and end dates. This count is used for balance sufficiency checks, balance deductions, and balance restorations. The same formula applies everywhere the day count is derived from a date range. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest date range appears, not only here]

Before a LeaveRequest transitions from DRAFT to SUBMITTED, the system must verify: (1) startDate is not before the current date minus any applicable minimumNoticeDays from the associated LeavePolicy; (2) endDate >= startDate; (3) the employee's LeaveBalance for the relevant policy and fiscal year has remainingDays >= the requested day count; (4) the employee's employmentStatus is ACTIVE; (5) the LeavePolicy is ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest is submitted, if the associated LeavePolicy has a non-null minimumNoticeDays, then startDate must be >= (submissionDate + minimumNoticeDays). The submissionDate is the date on which the submit() transition executes. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission — minimum notice appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and fiscal year must have its usedDays increased by the request's day count, and remainingDays recalculated as totalEntitlement - usedDays. This is an atomic operation — the balance update and status transition must succeed or fail together. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance deduction on approval appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions from APPROVED to CANCELLED, the employee's LeaveBalance must have its usedDays decreased by the request's day count, and remainingDays recalculated. The balance must never go below zero. This restoration is atomic with the cancellation transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance restoration on cancellation from APPROVED appears, not only here]

Only the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a LeaveRequest. If the employee has no manager (managerId is null), the request escalates to an HR admin role. The system must not allow self-approval. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval — manager authorisation appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest may be cancelled by: (1) the owning employee, at any non-terminal state; (2) the employee's manager, at any non-terminal state; (3) an HR admin, at any non-terminal state. Cancellation from APPROVED triggers balance restoration. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation — authorisation appears, not only here]

The fiscal year for a LeaveBalance is derived from the LeaveRequest's startDate. The fiscal year runs from January 1 to December 31. A request with a startDate in 2026 maps to fiscalYear 2026, regardless of endDate. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance fiscal year appears, not only here]

For a given (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) tuple, there must be at most one LeaveBalance with status ACTIVE. When a new fiscal year begins, a new ACTIVE balance is created and the previous year's balance transitions to CLOSED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance — one active balance per employee per policy per fiscal year appears, not only here]

An employee must not have two APPROVED LeaveRequests with overlapping date ranges. Overlap is defined as: requestA.startDate <= requestB.endDate AND requestB.startDate <= requestA.endDate. This check runs on submission and on approval. Overlapping DRAFT or REJECTED requests are permitted. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest — no overlapping approved requests appears, not only here]

When a LeavePolicy has requiresManagerApproval = false, LeaveRequests of that type transition directly from SUBMITTED to APPROVED without manager intervention. The approvedBy and approvedAt fields remain null. All other submission validations (balance sufficiency, date validity, no overlaps, employee active, policy active) still apply. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval appears, not only here]

remainingDays must never be negative. Any operation that would cause remainingDays < 0 (e.g. approval when balance is insufficient, or a bug in restoration arithmetic) must be rejected as a domain error before the balance is mutated. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance.remainingDays appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — state machine with strict transition rules. APPROVED → CANCELLED triggers balance restoration.
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — governs whether the policy applies to new requests.
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, CLOSED — one ACTIVE balance per (employee, policy, fiscalYear). CLOSED on fiscal year rollover.
- **Employee**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED — only ACTIVE employees may submit leave.

## Key domain invariants

- remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays, never negative.
- Day count = (endDate - startDate) + 1, inclusive, applied uniformly.
- No overlapping APPROVED LeaveRequests for the same employee.
- Balance deduction on approval and restoration on cancellation-from-approved are atomic with the status transition.
- Only the employee's manager (or HR admin when no manager) may approve/reject; no self-approval.
- requiresManagerApproval = false policies auto-approve on submission (all other validations still apply).
- At most one ACTIVE LeaveBalance per (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear).

## Open questions for chief architect

1. Fiscal year definition (calendar vs custom).
2. Cross-fiscal-year LeaveRequest handling (pro-rate, single-year charge, or reject).
3. Calendar days vs business days for leave counting.
4. Accrual model (lump sum, monthly pro-rata, per-pay-period, or configurable).
5. Whether emergency leave bypasses minimumNoticeDays.

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal year definition — calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) or a custom period (e.g. Apr 1 – Mar 31)?
open_questions.impact: Determines which LeaveBalance a LeaveRequest maps to when startDate and endDate span a fiscal year boundary. Affects balance sufficiency checks and the fiscalYear derivation logic.
candidate_options: Custom: configurable per organisation (e.g. Apr 1 – Mar 31)

open_questions.question: How should a LeaveRequest whose date range spans two fiscal years be handled?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance sufficiency checks, deduction logic, and whether a single LeaveRequest can touch two LeaveBalance records. The current domain model assumes one balance per request; spanning years would require multi-balance deduction.
candidate_options: Pro-rate: split the request across two fiscal years, checking and deducting from each year's balance independently
Single-year: the entire request is charged to the fiscal year of the startDate
Reject: requests spanning fiscal years are not allowed

open_questions.question: Should leave day counting use calendar days or business days?
open_questions.impact: Directly affects the day-count formula, balance sufficiency checks, and how employees plan leave. Calendar days is simpler but may be unfair for long leaves spanning weekends. Business days requires a holiday calendar.
candidate_options: Calendar days: all days in the range count, including weekends and holidays
Business days + holidays: weekends and a configurable holiday calendar excluded

open_questions.question: How does leave entitlement accrue — lump sum at fiscal year start, monthly pro-rata, or per-pay-period?
open_questions.impact: Determines when LeaveBalance.totalEntitlement is set and whether partial-year employees get pro-rated entitlement. Affects balance initialisation logic and the accrual scheduler.
candidate_options: Annual accrual: full entitlement granted at start of fiscal year
Monthly pro-rata: entitlement/12 granted each month
Per-pay-period: entitlement divided across pay periods

open_questions.question: Does emergency leave bypass the minimumNoticeDays constraint?
open_questions.impact: Affects the submission validation logic. Emergency leave is typically for unforeseen circumstances; enforcing a notice period contradicts its purpose.
candidate_options: Emergency leave always bypasses minimumNoticeDays regardless of policy setting
Emergency leave bypasses minimumNoticeDays only if the policy explicitly sets minimumNoticeDays to null
No special bypass — emergency leave follows the same rules as other types
